title: Network Shield templates: subnet profiles & egress policy Terraform module
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a composable Terraform module (Network Shield Templates) that expresses tenant-safe subnet profiles, zone affinity, egress policy abstraction (NAT/IGW selection by workload class), and first-class interface for VPC Endpoints and routing rules. Deliverables should include upgrade hooks, a lightweight health-checking mechanism for egress endpoints, and migration tooling for existing private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Module supports parameterized subnet profiles (control-plane, shared-services, workload-primary, workload-burst) with CIDR tiling and AZ-aware allocation
Egress policy abstraction allows per-subnet policy: 'managed-nat', 'internet-gateway', or 'private-only' with explicit fallback rules
VPC endpoint configuration supports service-scoped endpoints (S3, STS, ECR) and private DNS toggle per-environment
Routing tables and route propagation are generated deterministically and include safety guards to prevent accidental 0.0.0.0/0 attachments without explicit opt-in
Module exposes a canary/rolling upgrade plan using a health-probe lambda + SSM parameter hook that gates major changes
Automated health checks report to Console (via metrics endpoint) and generate actionable alerts for stuck egress attachments
Documentation and example stacks for single-tenant and multi-tenant deployments included in repo
Unit tests (terraform validate + terratest subset) and a CI workflow that verifies idempotence and drift protection
tasks: Design schema for subnet profiles and CIDR tiling (owner: Liam)
Implement VPC endpoint templating with private DNS toggle
Add routing safety checks and explicit opt-in flags
Create upgrade hook (lambda health prober) and SSM/Parameter interface
Write terratest scenarios for single-AZ, multi-AZ, and multi-tenant overlays
Author docs and migration playbook (Confluence + README examples)
Open PR and run internal canary in staging for two weeks
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after operations runbook review. Current gap: no single module supports workload-class egress selection and safe upgrades across Private customers.

2026-03-03 - Liam O'Connor: Initial design spike completed. Decided to represent subnet profiles as a small list of typed maps to keep HCL ergonomics while enabling validation. Draft schema pushed to branch feature/ENG-770123-schema.

2026-03-04 - Design review (Maya Chen): Recommended clearer naming for 'workload-burst' to avoid confusion with autoscaling; proposal to instead use 'ephemeral-workload' profile. Added label 'multitenancy'.

2026-03-05 - Engineering note: Chose to prefer explicit NAT gateway resources when 'managed-nat' selected; for cost-sensitive environments allow a "shared-nat" option (reference existing shared NAT pattern in infra repo).
2026-03-06 - Security (Ravi Kaur): Requested explicit policy and audit hooks for VPC endpoint creation (IAM role assumption and KMS key reference). Security review required=true.

2026-03-08 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype health-probe lambda implemented; it performs TCP connect + route table verification and writes status to SSM parameter and CloudWatch metric namespace 'NetworkShield/Health'. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/6421

2026-03-09 - QA (Jin Park): Terratest smoke for AZ alignment passed in staging. Noted failure when module receives overlapping CIDR inputs; added validation step to fail-fast with a clear error message.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Add migration playbook stub: three-step plan (snapshot route tables, deploy side-by-side subnets, cutover routes with canary traffic) and rollback steps. Link to playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Network+Shield+Migration+Playbook
notes: Trade-offs: We intentionally avoid building service mesh-level egress policies in this module — goal is infra-level attachment and routing only. Application-layer egress controls should be implemented by product teams or via later console features.
Compatibility: Aim for Terraform 1.5+ compatibility and AWS provider v5.x. Keep HCL2 friendly patterns so customers can fork with minimal changes.
Rollout plan: Deploy to dedicated staging org; run synthetic egress probes for 7 days; enabled canary flag for 10% of traffic in production account before full cutover.
Follow-ups: add RBAC audit exporter for endpoint creations and a small operator-runner that can reconcile NAT attachments if drift is detected.
